userStories.title: Stop edge functions leaking error stack traces / raw messages to clients
userStories.description: As the platform, no edge function should return a JavaScript stack trace or raw driver/error message in its HTTP response — those leak file paths, internal table/function names, package versions and sometimes secrets to any caller. Route every 5xx through the existing sanitized responder.
acceptanceCriteria: No edge function returns error.stack in any HTTP response body. The audited offenders (gsc-sync-data, crawl-site, send-seo-notification, seo-audit, run-scheduled-audit, search-new-restaurants, analyze-content, analyze-images) have their top-level catch handlers converted to _shared/errorResponse.ts errorResponse(), which returns a generic client message and removes the paired raw error.message
Server-side logging of the full error (including stack via console.error / the helper's own log) is retained — sanitization is client-facing only
HTTP status codes on those handlers are unchanged so existing web/mobile clients that branch on a status keep working (CLAUDE.md backward-compat); the response still carries a string `error` field
console.error('...stack...', error.stack) used purely for server logs is left as-is (not a client leak)
grep for `error.stack` / `err.stack` inside Response/JSON.stringify bodies across supabase/functions returns nothing; npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: DONE (2026-06-25): converted the 8 audited functions' top-level catch handlers from returning {error: error.message, details: error.stack} to the existing _shared/errorResponse.ts errorResponse() helper (WEB-SEC-007 pattern): gsc-sync-data, crawl-site, send-seo-notification, seo-audit, run-scheduled-audit, analyze-content, analyze-images (identical block) + search-new-restaurants (which also leaked a dev-gated stack). Each now returns a generic sanitized `error` string with the SAME 500 status and CORS headers; the full error + stack is still logged server-side (errorResponse console.error + the functions' own console.error). VERIFIED: grep shows no error.stack/err.stack inside any Response/JSON.stringify body across supabase/functions (the only remaining hit is search-new-restaurants' server-side console.error('Error details', {stack}) log, which is correct); all 8 files esbuild-parse clean; npm run validate exits 0. Backward-compat: status codes unchanged, response still carries a string `error` field, no request-shape change. OUT OF SCOPE (documented in story): per-item error.message strings inside admin-authenticated batch-result arrays (social-media-manager, scrape-events, etc.) — diagnostic output, not a secret leak.

userStories.title: Require admin/trigger auth on campaign-creative-review
userStories.description: As the platform, the campaign-creative-review edge function (AI creative scoring, WEB-AUTO-010) builds a service-role client and runs cost-bearing AI work but has no caller authorization — any party that can reach it can trigger reviews (cost/DoS, metric manipulation). Gate it like the other admin/internal functions while keeping the DB-trigger path working.
acceptanceCriteria: campaign-creative-review rejects callers that are not an admin/root_admin JWT or the service-role key (reuse requireAdminOrApiKey from _shared, which already accepts the SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY bearer the DB trigger sends)
The existing insert-trigger invocation path still succeeds (it sends the service-role key), verified against how the trigger calls the function
No request/response shape change on the authorized path (backward-compat for the trigger + admin UI)
Unauthorized calls get a 401/403 with a generic message (no internals leaked)
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: DONE (2026-06-25): added `await requireAdminOrApiKey(req, corsHeaders)` (from _shared/apiKeyAuth.ts) at the top of the campaign-creative-review handler, right after CORS. The helper accepts EDGE_FUNCTION_API_KEY (header/bearer), the SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY bearer, or an admin/root_admin JWT; on failure it returns a sanitized 401/403. VERIFIED the trigger path still works: migration 20260620000006_creative_auto_review.sql invokes the function from BOTH the AFTER INSERT trigger (enqueue_creative_review) and the */10 cron sweep using `Authorization: Bearer <service_role_key>` — exactly the service-role branch requireAdminOrApiKey allows (apiKeyAuth.ts:118-121). No src/ caller exists (admin UI never invokes it directly); autonomy-overview only references the name as a job_name string, not an invocation. Backward-compat: authorized request/response shapes unchanged; get_active_ads and campaign/advertisement shapes untouched (iOS unaffected). esbuild parses clean; npm run validate exits 0.

userStories.title: Fix recommendation N+1 + detail-page column over-fetch
userStories.description: As a user, recommendation and detail surfaces should issue tight, batched, column-projected queries instead of per-item N+1 loops and select('*') over wide tables, to cut payloads and latency toward the PERF budgets.
acceptanceCriteria: useSimplePersonalization.combineAndScoreRecommendations no longer issues one query per trending item in a loop — it groups candidate ids by content_type and batch-fetches with .in('id', ids) (parallel per type); recommendation order, scores, preference boost and dedup are unchanged
useSimplePersonalization.getPopularContent fetches its candidate tables in parallel (Promise.all) instead of sequential awaits, then fills in the same table-priority order (behavior preserved)

AttractionDetails main lookup no longer downloads every full attraction row to slug-match — it scans only (id, name), then fetches the single matched attraction's full row by id (SEO/GEO content intact)
RestaurantDetails + AttractionDetails related/nearby CARD queries project explicit *_LIST_COLUMNS (the SEO/GEO-bearing main detail row stays select('*') per the listColumns.ts design note)
No change to rendered fields or ordering on any surface; npm run validate passes
userStories.notes:
DONE (2026-06-25). Scoped to safe, high-value wins; deliberately did NOT narrow the SEO/GEO-bearing main detail queries (listColumns.ts documents detail pages keep full rows for SEO).
- useSimplePersonalization.ts combineAndScoreRecommendations: was a per-item select('*').eq('id').single() inside a for-loop (N sequential round-trips). Now dedups candidates, groups ids by content_type, batch-fetches each type with .in('id', ids) via Promise.all, then rebuilds in original trending order with the same score/boost. Content shape kept (select('*')) so no consumer breaks. Minor, more-correct nuance: a candidate whose row is missing is simply skipped (and was already de-duped), so getPopularContent won't re-surface it.
- getPopularContent: 4 sequential per-table select('*') awaits → Promise.all parallel fetch, then fill in the same table order (events,restaurants,attractions,playgrounds) preserving the cap/dedup.
- AttractionDetails main query: previously select('*') over the ENTIRE attractions table to find one by createSlug(name). Now selects only (id,name) to find the match, then one select('*').eq('id') for the full row → bulk scan shrinks from full-rows to id+name pairs, SEO/GEO preserved.
- RestaurantDetails related+nearby and AttractionDetails related+nearby card queries → RESTAURANT_LIST_COLUMNS / ATTRACTION_LIST_COLUMNS (same sets the list views/cards already use, WEB-PERF-001).
VERIFIED: npm run type-check + validate exit 0 (non-literal column-string constants return a loose type compatible with the card components, same as WEB-PERF-001 usage).

userStories.title: Persist adapter-provided image_url at event ingest (firecrawl-scraper)
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I want scraped events to keep the image the domain adapters already fetched, because firecrawl-scraper drops item.image_url when building the events insert — so SeatGeek / Funny Bone / Catch Des Moines events land with image_url=NULL even though the image was already available.
acceptanceCriteria: The events branch of transformedData (supabase/functions/firecrawl-scraper/index.ts ~1029-1047) includes image_url sourced from item.image_url when present; the restaurants/attractions branches likewise pass through item.image_url when their adapter provides one

Adapter-provided images go through the existing SSRF/dimension-guarded fetchAndStoreImage path (mirroring ai-crawler) so remote URLs are validated and stored rather than hot-linked blindly; on fetch/validation failure the event still inserts with image_url NULL (no regression)
image_url is only set when the item actually carries one — no behavior change for adapters that return image_url:null (barnstormers, milb, sports-schedule rows)
BACKWARD COMPAT: additive only — no request/response shape change to firecrawl-scraper, and event read shapes older iOS/Android binaries consume are unchanged (CLAUDE.md)
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: Evidence: seatgeek.ts:142 (performer image), catchdesmoines.ts:303 (ld+json image), eventbrite.ts:176, hyveetix.ts:349 all already return item.image_url on ScrapedItem (types.ts:19), but the events transformedData object at firecrawl-scraper/index.ts:1029-1047 omits image_url entirely, so every adapter's image is silently discarded at insert. ai-crawler already demonstrates the fetchAndStoreImage SSRF/dimension guard to copy from. LIVE DB: 253/286 upcoming events (88%) have image_url NULL; 190 are seatgeek.com and every Funny Bone row is SeatGeek adapter output whose image was fetched then thrown away. CAVEAT: the SeatGeek image is the performer photo (shared across all dates of a tour/homestand) — correct for concerts/comedy, venue-plausible otherwise; scraping each SeatGeek event page is NOT viable (JS shells that never yield an image). userStories.notes: FROM WEB CODE REVIEW 2026-07-11. Evidence: 385 any occ / 127 files; SearchTrafficDashboard.tsx (20). Depends on WEB-DB-003. | RESOLVED 2026-07-18 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes). Repo-wide typed-any occurrences (: any | as any | <any> | any[]) went 397 -> 357 against the branch base 64013afc, concentrated in the files this story names. SearchTrafficDashboard.tsx 12 -> 0, contentValidation.ts 7 -> 0, security/ownership.ts 7 -> 2 (the two survivors are generic query-builder helpers where the cast is genuinely load-bearing). THE IMPORTANT PART IS NOT THE COUNT — typing security/ownership.ts uncovered a real latent defect. getTableName was typed Record<OwnableResource, string>, and retyping its values to keyof Database[public][Tables] made the compiler reveal that SIX of fifteen entries pointed at tables that DO NOT EXIST: reviews, ratings, favorites, advertisements, saved_itineraries, event_alerts. isResourceOwner would query the nonexistent table, get an error, and hit `if (error || !data) return false` — so every ownership check for those six resource types silently denied. It fails CLOSED, so not a vulnerability, but it would have broken legitimate actions (a user unable to edit their own review) the moment the module was used. It went unnoticed because useResourceOwnership currently has ZERO consumers — the whole module is dead code today. Three were renames and are now mapped correctly after verifying each carries the user_id column OWNERSHIP_COLUMNS expects: review -> event_reviews, rating -> user_ratings, favorite -> content_favorites. The other three are mapped to null and NOT guessed: advertisement, trip_plan, event_alert have no identified equivalent (curated_itineraries and advertising_packages exist but are editorial/pricing tables, not per-user records). Guessing here is the dangerous direction — an ownership check against a table whose user_id belongs to a different entity could fail OPEN — whereas null makes isResourceOwner log an explicit error and deny. THESE THREE MUST BE RESOLVED BEFORE THIS MODULE IS WIRED INTO ANYTHING. Also added getErrorMessage(error: unknown) to lib/errorHandler.ts so catch blocks can be typed `catch (error)` (which TS types as unknown) rather than `catch (error: any)` purely to reach .message; it handles Error instances, bare strings and PostgREST/Supabase rejections, which are plain objects and not Errors. 38 `catch (x: any)` sites remain across 12 other files and can now be converted incrementally against that helper. contentValidation validators are now typed Partial<Row> off the generated schema — deliberately Partial, since they validate unverified submissions where fields legitimately may be missing, while still constraining field NAMES (a typo like event.titel previously validated clean and reported the field as missing).

userStories.title: Advance the strictNullChecks migration and add a strict type-check CI gate
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the strict-TS migration to progress and hold, because tsconfig.json has strictNullChecks/noImplicitAny off and tsconfig.strict.json includes only ~10 files with no CI gate, so strictness never expands.
acceptanceCriteria: A batch of additional already-compliant files is added to tsconfig.strict.json include

Backward-compat per CLAUDE.md: no edge-function request/response shape changes, no tightened validation/rate limits, DB changes additive-only across releases
npm run validate passes with no new errors
userStories.notes: FROM WEB CODE REVIEW 2026-07-11. Evidence: tsconfig.json (strictNullChecks:false); tsconfig.strict.json includes ~10 files; no CI gate. | RESOLVED 2026-07-18 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes) — but AC1 was implemented differently to how it was written, because the mechanism it describes does not work. THE PREMISE WAS WRONG. AC1 asks for "a batch of additional already-compliant files added to tsconfig.strict.json include", on the stated evidence that the config "includes only ~10 files". But `include` does NOT bound what TypeScript checks — tsc checks every file reachable by import from those roots. The nine listed roots were already pulling in and reporting errors across 59 files. Adding more roots does not tighten the gate; it usually pulls MORE non-compliant files into the graph and makes the count go UP. So that AC as written would have made things worse. THE CONFIG COULD NOT PASS AT ALL: 273 errors on the first run. Diagnosis: 185 of those came from four checks that have nothing to do with strictNullChecks — noUncheckedIndexedAccess, noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature, noUnusedLocals and noUnusedParameters. 78 were TS4111 alone, which only asks that obj.foo be written obj["foo"] on index-signature types. That volume of mechanical noise buried the genuine null-safety failures, which is a large part of why this migration never moved. Split the config into TIER 1 (the checks this story is actually about: strictNullChecks, noImplicitAny, strictFunctionTypes and friends) and a documented, deliberately deferred TIER 2 carrying those four. Tier 1 alone: 273 -> 88 errors across 27 files — a tractable number. ENFORCEMENT IS A RATCHET, NOT A PASS/FAIL GATE. Added scripts/strict-ratchet.mjs with a checked-in per-file baseline (strict-baseline.json, 88 errors / 27 files). It fails only if a file gets WORSE or a new file starts erroring, and prompts to re-baseline when things improve. Per-file rather than a single total on purpose: one number lets one file improve while another silently regresses, and this makes that trade visible and rejects it. A gate that can never pass just teaches everyone to ignore it; no gate at all lets the count drift. VERIFIED BY DELIBERATE REGRESSION, not just a clean run: injected `function __probe(x: string | null) { return x.length; }` into a baseline-clean file and confirmed the ratchet reports "src/hooks/useEventBySlug.ts: NEW" and exits 1, then passes again once reverted. CI: both `npm run check-imports` and `npm run type-check:strict:ratchet` added to the "Lint, Type Check, Test & Build" job in pr-checks.yml. That job is ALREADY in required_status_checks for main and develop, so these gate merges immediately rather than being non-blocking — the AC allowed non-blocking, but there was no reason to accept less given the ratchet cannot spuriously fail. Also added useEventBySlug.ts and useActiveAds.ts to the include list — both were written strict-clean earlier in this branch, which is the one case where extending the roots is genuinely correct. | PROGRESS 2026-07-18: baseline 88 -> 61 errors across 27 -> 25 files, and re-baselined so the ratchet holds the new line. Most of the reduction came from deleting 11 stale `.from("table" as string)` casts in useVoting, useExperiment, useFeatureFlag and useSceneUpdates. Those casts predated the WEB-DB-003 types regeneration and every table involved (voting_categories, votes, feature_flags, user_analytics, scene_updates) now exists, so the cast bought nothing — and cost a lot: casting the table name to `string` forces Supabase to consider every table overload, which is what produced the TS2589 "type instantiation is excessively deep" and the 245-way union errors. useVoting alone went 13 -> 0. Also fixed useVoting.image_url, typed `string` but nullable in the database. THE VALUABLE PART was not the count: chasing these surfaced a real user-facing defect, broken pagination on two list pages, filed and fixed as WEB-QA-014. That is the argument for this migration continuing — the remaining 61 are worth working through for what else they expose, not for the number. | PROGRESS 2026-07-18 (round 2): 61 -> 54 errors before the event-photo work, driven by useUserPreferences 7 -> 0. The pattern holding across this whole migration is that strict mode is not finding type nits, it is finding PHANTOM TABLES AND COLUMNS — code addressing schema that does not exist, always failing silently because the surrounding code swallows the error. So far: user_preferences (WEB-QA-015), event_discussions.message_type/media_url (WEB-QA-016), search_analytics column drift (WEB-QA-012), user_analytics.content_id (WEB-QA-013), the ownership table map (WEB-SEC-020), and broken pagination (WEB-QA-014). The TS2589 "type instantiation is excessively deep" error is the reliable signature: it means the table name did not resolve, so Supabase fell back to considering every table overload. | PROGRESS 2026-07-18 (round 3): 52 -> 38 errors across 24 -> 21 files, re-baselined. Playgrounds 7 -> 0, Header 6 -> 0, PlaygroundsMap 1 -> 0. No phantom-schema bugs this round — these were all genuine optional-vs-nullable mismatches, which is the other recurring shape: a hand-written interface declares `field?: string` while the column is `string | null`, so a row straight from the database does not satisfy the type the code claims to accept. Fixed by making the interfaces match the schema (PlaygroundsMap.Playground, UserMenu/MobileNav profile+userLevel+userXP) and by converting explicitly at component boundaries rather than loosening the shared target type (MapLocation.description stays `string | undefined`; the nullable column is coerced with ?? undefined at the call site). Also replaced two .filter(Boolean) calls with type predicates — .filter(Boolean) does not narrow `(string | null)[]` to `string[]` in TypeScript, so every downstream consumer still saw `| null`. THE RATCHET CAUGHT ME AGAIN: widening PlaygroundsMap.Playground.description to `string | null` broke its mapping into MapLocation, taking that file 1 -> 2, and the ratchet refused the commit until it was fixed properly at the boundary. Second time it has caught a regression in my own work. Verified /playgrounds, / and /events all still render with zero page errors.

userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-13 (5-PERSONA QA PASS — production live; persona: Marcus / weekend dad). SEVERITY: HIGH — breaks the core events flow and torches trust. Evidence: Family filter returns 1 result; clicking it navigates to the slug above and shows the 'Event Not Found — This event may have ended or been removed' state. Likely related to WEB-QA-003 (events querying is unhealthy). Note the surfaced event is also dated 2026-10-01 (~3 months out) which is a separate content-freshness concern, not the bug here. | RESOLVED 2026-07-18 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes). Root cause: EventDetails had no detail query at all — it called useEvents() (unbounded, extra visibility filters) and did a client-side Array.find over a slug computed from each row, so any row the list showed but that hook did not return 404d. Two independent failure modes: (1) predicate asymmetry — the list applied neither is_merged nor is_hidden while useEvents applied both; (2) the unbounded fetch was silently truncated at PostgREST max-rows, so far-future events were never in the array. Fix: new src/hooks/useEventBySlug.ts does a bounded server-side lookup, parsing the -YYYY-MM-DD off the slug and querying only that date window with the SAME visibility predicates as the list; EventsPage list now also applies .neq(is_merged)/.neq(is_hidden). NOTE for future work: events.date is a timestamptz, not a DATE — an inclusive `.lte(date, YYYY-MM-DD)` bound resolves to midnight and drops same-day evening events (an evening-Central event stores as the next day in UTC). Uses an exclusive `.lt` upper bound one day past the window. Covered by tests/route-smoke.spec.ts, which caught exactly that timestamptz case on a real row.

userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-13 (5-PERSONA QA PASS — production live). SEVERITY: N/A (coverage gap). The persona pass (Marcus/mobile dad, Priya/newcomer, Gary/skeptic, Zoe/power user, Diana/business owner) covered homepage, events list+detail+filters, trip-planner, restaurants, pricing, auth, and theme toggle, but could not verify: true mobile viewport rendering (window stayed desktop-width), any authenticated feature (no account created — signup is out of scope for automated QA), contact/reviews submission, Stripe checkout, and SEO landing/attractions/articles pages. | RESOLVED 2026-07-18 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes) — with one AC explicitly NOT covered; see below. MOBILE RENDERING (AC1) VERIFIED: swept 14 routes x 3 viewports (320x568, 375x667 iPhone SE, 393x851 Pixel 5) with isMobile/hasTouch, measuring document overflow, error boundaries and HTTP status. Found real horizontal overflow on SIX routes at EVERY phone width - /events, /restaurants, /attractions, /articles, /playgrounds, /neighborhoods - up to 215px at 320px wide. Root-caused and FIXED as WEB-QA-008 (FAQ accordion questions could not wrap because the shadcn Button base sets whitespace-nowrap). The sweep went from 18 problematic combinations to 1 after the fix, the survivor being a 1px rounding artifact. Mobile nav verified: bottom nav present on every sampled route, labelled hamburger present everywhere except /auth (appears intentional). Touch targets measured and filed as WEB-QA-009. SEO LANDING + SECONDARY SECTIONS (AC4) VERIFIED: /events/today, /restaurants/open-now, /attractions, /articles, /playgrounds, /neighborhoods all return 2xx and mount without an error boundary at all three phone widths. B2B/CONTACT SURFACES (AC3) PARTIALLY VERIFIED: /advertise, /business-partnership and /contact all mount cleanly at phone widths (/advertise only because WEB-QA-001 fixed its React #130 crash earlier in this same branch). NOT verified: actual contact-form SUBMISSION and the reviews moderation UI - both require either sending real data to production or an authenticated admin session. LOGGED-IN FLOWS (AC2) NOT VERIFIED AT ALL. This is the significant coverage gap and it is unchanged from the original persona pass. Free-tier limits (3 favorites, 0 alerts/saved searches), saved searches, review submission with AI auto-moderation (WEB-AUTO-009) and social sharing all require an authenticated account. The story notes state signup is out of scope for automated QA, and creating an account against the production database is not something to do unilaterally. Everything behind auth therefore remains unconfirmed and needs a human pass or a seeded test account. STATIC ANALYSIS FOUND SOMETHING THE SWEEP ALONE WOULD NOT HAVE: while verifying the favorites surface, the regenerated types showed the favorites write path and read path target different tables (filed as WEB-QA-010) - so even a manual logged-in pass of AC2 would likely find restaurant/attraction favorites silently broken. DEFECTS FILED PER AC5: WEB-QA-008 (mobile overflow, MED, fixed), WEB-QA-009 (touch targets, LOW-MED), WEB-QA-010 (favorites read/write mismatch, MED), WEB-QA-011 (get_rotated_restaurants inconsistent total_count, LOW), WEB-QA-012 (search_analytics 42703, LOW), WEB-SEC-020 (unmapped ownership resource types, MED latent). METHOD NOTE: naive overflow detection is misleading and cost two wrong diagnoses before the real one. Carousel children inside an overflow-x:auto container legitimately extend past the viewport, and position:fixed elements with inset-x-0 size to the EXPANDED layout viewport, so they report widths of exactly viewport + overflow and look like the biggest offenders while actually being symptoms. Any future overflow hunt must exclude clipped ancestors and fixed subtrees before ranking candidates.

The widest overflowing nodes were carousel children inside a legitimate overflow-x:auto container (fine by design), and then position:fixed elements with inset-x-0 (cookie banner, bottom nav, toast viewport) whose widths were exactly 375 + docOverflow - they stretch to the expanded layout viewport, so they are symptoms of the overflow rather than causes. userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-18 during WEB-QA-007 mobile verification (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes). SEVERITY: LOW-MED. Measured at 375x667 with isMobile/hasTouch: 9-22 sub-44px interactive elements per page (/ 11, /events 22, /restaurants 21, /pricing 9, /auth 11). NOTE ON STANDARD: WCAG 2.1 AA (2.5.8) requires only 24x24, which these mostly meet, so this is NOT an AA failure - 44x44 is WCAG AAA (2.5.5) and the Apple/Google platform guidance. CLAUDE.md states a mobile-first, touch-targets-first standard, which is why this is filed. A repo .touch-target utility (min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px]) already exists and is the intended fix. Mobile nav verified working: bottom nav present on all sampled routes and a labelled hamburger present everywhere except /auth, which appears intentional. | PARTIAL 2026-07-18 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes) — LEFT passes:false ON PURPOSE. The AC asks for a 44x44 minimum across mobile controls; what landed covers the highest-traffic ones, not all of them, so claiming this story is done would be false. WHAT WAS FIXED. Added a .tap-area-44 utility that overlays a centred, invisible 44x44 hit region via ::after instead of growing the element. That distinction matters: the pre-existing .touch-target utility works by enlarging the control itself, which is wrong for icon-sized controls — a 24px close button or 36px social icon would visibly change size and reflow the surrounding layout. The overlay is scoped to (pointer: coarse) so a mouse never gets an expanded region that could overlap adjacent controls. Applied to the header logo (32x32), the cookie banner close button (24x24) and the three footer social links (36x36). VERIFIED: each still RENDERS at its original size while its effective tap area measures 44x44. Separately bumped min-h-[44px] on the event date-preset chips (were 92x38), the restaurant quick chips, and the Event/Restaurant inline category filters (were 122x38) — verified live, "Today" now measures 92x44. WHAT IS NOT FIXED, AND WHY THE STORY STAYS OPEN. Dozens of controls remain under 44px, spread across many components — pagination links, sort/select triggers, "Load More" buttons, newsletter inputs (mostly 36-42px tall with adequate width) and a long tail of icon buttons. Fixing them all is a broad sweep across shared components with real desktop-regression risk, and it was not attempted here. ONE CATEGORY SHOULD BE CLOSED AS A DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION RATHER THAN FIXED: roughly 21 per page are inline text links inside running copy (Privacy Policy 65x15, footer nav links 89x19, the contact email 155x16, "Forgot password?" 110x20, breadcrumb "Home" 38x20). WCAG 2.5.8 explicitly exempts inline links in a block of text, and enlarging them would break line flow; applying the overlay to them would be actively harmful, since it would collide with neighbouring text and steal its clicks. That reasoning is recorded in the utility comment in index.css so nobody applies it there later. ALSO STILL OPEN from this story AC: the residual 1px horizontal overflow on /attractions at 320px is unchanged (the 42-combination sweep still reports exactly that one item, down from 18 before WEB-QA-008). | COMPLETED 2026-07-18 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes), second pass. Measured inventory of distinct sub-44px-height controls across /, /events, /restaurants, /attractions, /pricing and /auth went 15 -> 5, and all 5 survivors are the documented-exception category (below). THE LEVERAGE WAS IN THE SHARED PRIMITIVES, not in individual pages. Added a `coarse:` Tailwind variant (@media (pointer: coarse)) and applied `coarse:min-h-[44px]` to the shadcn Button default/sm sizes, Input, and the Select trigger. That one change fixed 8 of the 15 at once. The variant matters: a blanket min-height would have visibly loosened dense admin and toolbar layouts on desktop, which is presumably why nobody wanted to touch these primitives before. Verified both directions — on desktop (pointer: fine) the overlay computes to display:none and control heights are unchanged; on mobile the select trigger measures 44 and the overlay is active. FOR CONTROLS THAT CANNOT GROW, used the .tap-area-44 overlay from the first pass (invisible centred 44x44 ::after, coarse-pointer only): the pricing Switch (24px tall by design — a taller switch would look wrong beside its label) and the card FavoriteButton (36x36, sits on card imagery in a fixed corner, so growing it would cover the photo and shift the badges). FOLLOWED THE EXISTING CONVENTION RATHER THAN ADDING A SECOND ONE: the Restaurants view-mode toggles were 32x32, and I first applied the overlay — then found EventsPage already solves the identical widget with `h-11 w-11 sm:h-8 sm:w-8` (44px on mobile, compact on desktop). Reverted to match that pattern, since two different solutions for the same widget is worse than either one. THE 5 REMAINING ARE A DELIBERATE, DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION — four are text links styled as text ("Events" in the footer, "View All Featured", the "Home" breadcrumb, and "Forgot password?"), all 20px tall. WCAG 2.5.8 AA explicitly exempts inline links in a block of text, these already meet the 24x24 AA floor in the axis that matters, and enlarging them would break line flow. Applying the overlay to them would be actively harmful — it would collide with adjacent text and steal its clicks, which is warned about in the utility comment in index.css. The fifth is a whole-card <a> at 42px, 2px short, where the entire card is already the tap area. ALSO CLOSED FROM THIS STORY AC: nothing changed for the residual 1px overflow on /attractions at 320px — the 42-combination sweep still reports exactly that one item and it remains a sub-pixel rounding artifact, not a layout defect. Build clean, validate clean, strict ratchet holding at the 88-error baseline.

userStories.title: Favorites write path and read path target different tables, so restaurant/attraction favorites never appear
userStories.description: As a signed-in user, I need my saved favorites to show up in My Favorites, because the button that saves them writes to a different table than the view that lists them.
acceptanceCriteria: Identify the canonical favorites table (content_favorites appears to be the intended destination) and migrate reads and writes onto it
useFavorites (used by every FavoriteButton) currently writes ONLY to user_event_interactions
FavoritesView reads user_restaurant_interactions and user_attraction_interactions; the latter does not exist in the schema at all
Restaurant and attraction favorites round-trip end to end after the fix
Backward-compat per CLAUDE.md: additive-only DB changes, dual-write across releases if the storage table changes
userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-18 during WEB-DB-003 types regeneration (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes). SEVERITY: MED - a shipped feature that silently does nothing for two of three content types. Evidence: src/hooks/useFavorites.ts queries only user_event_interactions (lines 23, 42, 86). src/components/FavoritesView.tsx reads user_restaurant_interactions (line ~55) and user_attraction_interactions (line ~82). The regenerated types.ts confirms user_attraction_interactions does not exist, so that query always errors; the code swallows it via a debug log and returns [], which is why this never surfaced as a visible error. A generic content_favorites table exists and looks like the intended destination. The one remaining .from(... as any) cast in the codebase is on this line and is deliberately retained with an explanatory comment - do not remove it without fixing the write path first. | RESOLVED 2026-07-18 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes). CORRECTION TO MY OWN ROOT CAUSE ABOVE — the diagnosis I filed this story with was partly WRONG and the note is left in place rather than rewritten so the error is visible. I claimed useFavorites (used by every FavoriteButton) writes only to user_event_interactions, so neither read path could ever match. That is not right: FavoriteButton has TWO paths. EventFavoriteButton uses useFavorites -> user_event_interactions, but non-event content goes through a separate hook, useContentFavorites, which correctly writes to content_favorites with (user_id, content_type, content_id). So the WRITE side was never broken. THE ACTUAL DEFECT WAS READ-SIDE ONLY: FavoritesView queried user_restaurant_interactions (a table nothing writes to) and user_attraction_interactions (a table that does not exist at all), instead of content_favorites where the writes actually land. Both queries then swallowed their errors via a debug log and returned [], which is why saved restaurants and attractions silently never appeared and no error was ever visible. FIX: both queries now read content_favorites filtered by content_type. Implemented as a TWO-STEP fetch (collect content_ids, then select the content rows by .in("id", ids)) rather than an embedded join, because content_favorites.content_id is polymorphic — it points at whichever table content_type names — so there is no foreign key for PostgREST to traverse. Verified live: the embedded form `restaurants:content_id(*)` fails with PGRST200 "Could not find a relationship", while the two-step form returns OK against both restaurants and attractions. Errors are now logged with message/code/details/hint instead of being swallowed. This also removed the last `.from(... as any)` table cast in the codebase — it only existed to reference a table that does not exist, so WEB-DB-003 is now fully clean at 0 such casts. VERIFICATION LIMIT, STATED PLAINLY: the query shapes are verified against the live database and both steps return OK, but the full round-trip (favorite a restaurant, see it in My Favorites) needs an authenticated session with stored favorites. content_favorites currently returns 0 rows to an anonymous client, both because there is no seeded data and because RLS would hide other users rows regardless. That is the same authenticated-coverage gap tracked in WEB-QA-007 AC2 and it is NOT closed by this story.

userStories.title: Default rating filter silently hides every unrated restaurant (46 of 480)
userStories.description: As a visitor, I need the restaurants result count to be trustworthy, because the RPC backing the default sort reports a different total depending on the page size requested.
acceptanceCriteria: get_rotated_restaurants returns a total_count representing all matching rows, independent of limit_count/offset_count
Reproduce: same filters with limit_count 8 returns total_count 480, while limit_count 1000 returns 434 rows and total_count 434
Reconcile against the direct query count (480 non-merged restaurants) and determine which filter accounts for the 46-row difference
Backward-compat per CLAUDE.md: the RPC is called by shipped clients - behavioural fix only, no signature change
userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-18 during WEB-QA-004 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes). SEVERITY: LOW - the number currently rendered (434) does match the rows actually returned, so the UI is self-consistent; the defect is that total_count is entangled with the limit and so cannot be trusted as a real total. Fixing it needs a migration to the RPC, which is why it was not folded into WEB-QA-004. | RESOLVED 2026-07-18 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes) — AND THE PREMISE I FILED THIS STORY WITH WAS WRONG. The original note is left above rather than rewritten, so the mistake stays visible. This is the second story I filed with an incorrect root cause (see also WEB-QA-010). THE RPC IS FINE. get_rotated_restaurants uses COUNT(*) OVER () on the filtered set, which is limit-independent by construction. Called with identical filters at limit_count 8, 30, 500 and 1000 it returns total_count = 480 every single time. My original 480-vs-434 observation compared two different contexts — a node script against the browser — and I wrongly attributed the difference to limit_count. There was never a total_count bug. THE REAL DEFECT, which that wrong measurement happened to expose: the app ALWAYS sent min_rating and max_rating, because filters.rating defaults to [0, 5] and the code only checked `rating.length === 2` before forwarding it. The RPC predicate is `(min_rating IS NULL OR r.rating >= min_rating)`, and for a restaurant with a NULL rating that comparison evaluates to NULL, so the row is dropped. The "no filter" default therefore silently excluded every unrated restaurant. Exactly 46 of 480 — verified three ways: rating IS NULL count = 46, 480 - 434 = 46, and calling the RPC with min/max NULL returns 480 while min=0/max=5 returns 434. Those 46 are disproportionately the newest listings, so roughly 10% of inventory — including the freshest — was invisible on the default restaurants page. FIX IS CLIENT-SIDE, NO MIGRATION NEEDED (unlike what this story assumed): a hasRatingFilter() guard treats the full [0, 5] range as "not filtered" and sends NULL, on BOTH the RPC path and the direct-query fallback, which had the same bug via .gte/.lte. VERIFIED IN THE RUNNING APP: /restaurants now returns 480 rows with total_count 480 and the header reads "480 found" (was 434), and all 46 previously-hidden unrated restaurants are present in the payload. WORTH RECORDING: the strict-mode ratchet added in WEB-CI-007 immediately caught a regression in MY OWN fix — useRestaurants went 1 -> 5 errors because hasRatingFilter returned a plain boolean, which does not narrow `number[] | undefined` under strictNullChecks, so the `rating[0]` accesses right after it were unsafe. Converting it to a type predicate (`rating is [number, number]`) brought it back to the 88-error baseline. That is the ratchet doing exactly the job it was built for, on real work rather than an injected probe.

userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-18 during WEB-QUAL-004 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes). SEVERITY: MED (latent). Retyping getTableName from Record<OwnableResource, string> to the generated table-name union made the compiler reveal six entries pointing at nonexistent tables. Three were renames and are now fixed after verifying each carries user_id: review -> event_reviews, rating -> user_ratings, favorite -> content_favorites. The remaining three (advertisement, whose owner column is campaign_id; trip_plan; event_alert) have no identified equivalent - curated_itineraries and advertising_packages exist but are editorial/pricing tables, not per-user records - so they are mapped to null deliberately rather than guessed. null makes isResourceOwner log an explicit error and deny (fails closed, safe). Guessing a wrong table is the dangerous direction and could fail OPEN. The module is dead code today, which is the only reason this is not urgent. | RESOLVED 2026-07-18 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes) via the AC second option ("or the resource types are removed from OwnableResource"), and the module turned out to be considerably more broken than this story described. THE STORY SAID 3 OF 15 WERE BROKEN. Verifying every remaining pair against the LIVE schema — not just the generated types — found 7 of 15 were. Beyond the three with no table (advertisement, trip_plan, event_alert), four more had owner columns that do not exist: events.created_by, restaurants.claimed_by, attractions.created_by and discussion_replies.user_id all returned 42703. isResourceOwner would have errored and denied for those too, so the module could only ever have worked for 8 of the 15 types it advertised. EVENTS, RESTAURANTS AND ATTRACTIONS ARE NOT OWNABLE AT ALL. Dumped the full column list for each: there is no created_by, claimed_by, user_id or any equivalent. They are crawler-ingested editorial content that nobody owns in the database, so an ownership check on them cannot be expressed, never mind pass. Removed from OwnableResource rather than papered over. If a "claim your business" feature is wanted, it needs a schema change first — there is no claims table either. discussion_reply was a real fix rather than a removal: the column is created_by, not user_id. FINAL STATE: OwnableResource is down to 9 types, and ALL 9 are verified end to end against the live database — table exists AND owner column exists (review->event_reviews.user_id, rating->user_ratings.user_id, favorite->content_favorites.user_id, discussion->event_discussions.user_id, discussion_reply->discussion_replies.created_by, photo->event_photos.user_id, campaign->campaigns.user_id, profile->profiles.id, saved_search->saved_searches.user_id). The table map is typed Record<OwnableResource, TableName> with NO `| null`, so the compiler now rejects both a nonexistent table name and a null placeholder. IMPORTANT DISCOVERY FOR WHOEVER WIRES THIS UP — a server-side RPC already exists that does this job properly: user_owns_resource(p_table_name, p_resource_id, p_user_id, p_owner_column) returns boolean. Delegating isResourceOwner to it would be strictly better than maintaining a client-side table map: it is authoritative, it cannot drift out of sync with the schema the way this map did, and a client-side ownership check is advisory anyway since RLS is the real gate. That rewrite is a design change beyond this story AC, so it was not done here, but it is the recommended direction and useResourceOwnership still has zero consumers, so nothing is blocked by leaving it. userStories.title: Pagination controls on /restaurants and /attractions silently did nothing
userStories.description: As a visitor browsing past the first page, I need Load More / Next / Previous to work, because all three passed an updater function into a setter that only accepts a number, so the page never changed.
acceptanceCriteria: Load More, Next and Previous change the page on /restaurants and /attractions
The ?page= URL param carries a real number
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: FOUND AND FIXED 2026-07-18 (claude/web-qa-p1-fixes) while working down the WEB-CI-007 strict-mode backlog — this is a user-facing bug that the strict type-check surfaced and that nothing else had caught. SEVERITY: MED. ROOT CAUSE: `const setPage = (v: number) => setParam("page", v, { def: 1 })`, but six call sites across Attractions.tsx (L732, L745, L787) and Restaurants.tsx (L723, L736, L778) passed a React-style updater, e.g. setPage((p) => p + 1). setParam serialises with String(value), so the function SOURCE went into the URL — String((p)=>p+1) is literally "(p)=>p+1". getNum then parsed NaN and fell back to 1, so Load More, Next and Previous were all silent no-ops on both pages. The strict project reported it as TS2345 "Argument of type (p: any) => any is not assignable to parameter of type number"; the default tsconfig has the checks that would catch this turned off, which is why it shipped. FIX: setPage now accepts `number | ((prev: number) => number)` and resolves the updater against the current page, in Attractions, Restaurants and EventsPage (the last for consistency — it had the same signature but no updater call sites yet, so it was one edit away from the same bug). VERIFIED IN THE BROWSER: /restaurants Next now navigates to ?page=2 and Previous returns to page 1.

METHOD: enumerated all 248 public tables from the generated types and issued an anon-key SELECT against LIVE PRODUCTION for each — exactly what any visitor can do, since the anon key ships in the client bundle. Result: 40 tables returned real rows, 198 returned empty, 9 errored. MOST of the 40 are correctly public content (events, restaurants, attractions, playgrounds, articles, hotels, trails, venues, guides, pseo_pages, badges, subscription_plans). The concerns are the internal ones listed in the acceptance criteria. SEVERITY: MODERATE, and deliberately not overstated. NO PII and NO credentials were exposed. Every ai_environment_config default_value was checked for secret-shaped strings (sk-, eyJ, ghp_, AIza, xox) and none were found; the CLAUDE_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY rows have null defaults. restaurant_blacklist reasons are benign operational notes such as not-a-restaurant and gas-station, not defamatory. This is reconnaissance and control-defeat, not a breach. SHARPEST ITEM: blocked_email_domains at 5,361 rows. It is a security control whose effectiveness depends entirely on not being public, and it is public. TWO LIMITS ON THIS AUDIT, both important. (1) The 198 EMPTY results are AMBIGUOUS — an RLS-filtered table and a genuinely empty table are indistinguishable from anon, so this audit proves what IS exposed but CANNOT certify the rest is protected; a service-role row-count comparison is needed to separate them. (2) Only SELECT was tested. Anon INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE posture is UNVERIFIED and was deliberately not probed, because a write test against production could mutate real data. Close that gap against a staging database, not this one.

acceptanceCriteria: Add checkRateLimit to log-content-metrics, matching the other verify_jwt=false functions (geocode-location, image-transform, og-image and version-check are all rate-limited; this one is not)

userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps). METHOD: cross-referenced supabase/config.toml against every function body. 71 of 74 edge functions run verify_jwt=false, which is only safe when the function guards itself. 66 of the 71 do (requireApiKey / requireAdmin / requireAuth / requirePermission / withSecurity / secret comparison). THAT IS A GOOD RESULT and worth recording explicitly: WEB-SEC-001 largely worked. The five without an auth guard are geocode-location, image-transform, og-image, version-check and log-content-metrics — the first four are public by design AND rate-limited. log-content-metrics is the only one that is public by design and NOT rate-limited. SEVERITY: LOW-MODERATE, deliberately not inflated. Input validation is actually reasonable — content_type and metric_type are allowlisted and content_id must look like a UUID, so an attacker cannot write arbitrary shapes. The real gaps are the missing throttle, the uncapped events array, and the attacker-controlled metric_value. IMPACT IS BOUNDED BY WHAT CONSUMES THIS DATA: I traced every reader and found content_metrics feeds AdminAnalyticsDashboard.tsx and useContentTracking.ts. I found NO evidence it feeds trending_score, popularity_score, or any public ranking — so this is admin-analytics poisoning plus an unthrottled service-role write path, NOT ranking manipulation. If a future feature does wire content_metrics into ranking, re-rate this as HIGH before shipping it. CORRECTION WORTH KEEPING: an earlier pass of this audit flagged generate-seo-content as unguarded. That was a false positive in my own grep — it guards with requireApiKey (SEC-029) and rate-limits AI calls at max:10. The guard-name list had to be rebuilt from the actual _shared exports before the audit was trustworthy. | FIXED AND VERIFIED LOCALLY 2026-07-18. checkRateLimit added at 600/15min (deliberately loose: IP-keyed with no user identity, and the caller flushes every 10s = ~90 req/window PER TAB, so shared NAT would make a tight limit silently delete analytics for the busiest real traffic). Batch capped at 100 (excess sliced, not rejected — failing a whole batch would lose good data over one bad client). metric_value clamped to 0..1000. Endpoint stays unauthenticated, which is correct. Verified: deno check clean, tsc clean, clamp/cap logic exercised directly with 10 cases including Infinity/NaN/negatives plus a 50,000-event flood truncated to 100. ALSO FIXED a pre-existing deno check failure in the same file (declared union omitted the bare-array request shape) — confirmed pre-existing by checking the original before editing. passes stays false pending deploy + a post-deploy check that legitimate analytics still flow (watch for 429s from real traffic behind corporate NAT).

userStories.title: useAnalytics flush error path duplicated the queue instead of re-queueing failed events
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need the analytics queue to survive a failed flush without growing without bound, because the error path duplicated the wrong events and doubled the queue on every failure.
acceptanceCriteria: Failed events are re-queued; events enqueued during the flush are preserved once, not duplicated
The queue is bounded so a sustained backend outage cannot grow it without limit
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: FOUND AND FIXED 2026-07-18 while sizing rate limits for WEB-SEC-022. The catch block read [...eventQueue.current, ...eventQueue.current] under a comment saying it kept events for the next attempt. It did the opposite: eventsToFlush had already been cleared from the queue at the top of the try and was out of scope in the catch, so the events that actually failed were LOST, while anything enqueued during the in-flight flush was DUPLICATED — and duplicated again on each subsequent failure, doubling the queue each time. A backend outage therefore caused exponential memory growth in long-lived tabs plus inflated metric counts for whichever events survived. Fixed by hoisting eventsToFlush above the try so the catch can see it, re-queueing [...eventsToFlush, ...eventQueue.current], and bounding to MAX_QUEUED_EVENTS=500 (oldest dropped first — stale analytics matter less than a responsive page). Verified with tsc + eslint; the remaining eslint warnings in this file are pre-existing.

userStories.title: DECIDE BEFORE DEPLOY: event photos have two competing implementations, and the pending migration entrenches the weaker one
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need one event-photo implementation, because two exist, neither works, they do not share storage, and migration 20260718000003 is about to commit the codebase to the one with the weaker schema.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide which table owns event photos BEFORE applying 20260718000003, because that migration is the commitment point

Option A — keep event_discussions (what the migration does): photos become discussion rows with message_type=photo and media_url. Wins: one feed, comments and photos already interleave, migration is written and additive. Costs: no caption field distinct from message, no is_featured, and every photo query filters a general discussions table

Option B — adopt event_photos (already exists, purpose-built: caption, photo_url, is_featured, likes_count, event_id, user_id, and NOT NULL-clean): rewrite EventPhotoUpload/EventPhotoGallery/EventSocialHub against it and drop the migration. Wins: better-shaped schema, no overloading. Costs: rewrite of the live components, and the photo count in the social hub needs a second query
Whichever wins, DELETE the losing path rather than leaving it dormant — the dead path is what produced this ambiguity
Fix src/lib/security/ownership.ts:349, which maps resource type photo -> event_photos. If Option A wins, that mapping points at a table that will never hold a photo
Remove or repair useCommunityFeatures.getEventPhotos, which filters on event_photos.is_approved — a column that does not exist, so the query fails with 42703 on every call
schema-baseline.json shrinks by the event_photos.is_approved entry
userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps) while separating the fixable schema-baseline entries from the blocked ones. Of 84 baseline findings only 10 sit on tables that exist; 8 of those are crm_activities and are blocked behind WEB-QA-018 anyway. Chasing the last two is what surfaced this. THE TWO PATHS. Path A (LIVE): EventPhotoUpload -> event_discussions {message_type, media_url}, read by EventPhotoGallery, counted by EventSocialHub, mounted from EventDetails. Write currently fails with PGRST204 until 20260718000003 is applied (WEB-QA-016). Path B (DEAD): useCommunityFeatures.uploadEventPhoto/getEventPhotos -> event_photos. VERIFIED DEAD: zero callers anywhere in src/ (only the hook itself references it), and the live table holds ZERO rows. Its upload function is actually CORRECT — every column it inserts exists. Its read function is broken, filtering on is_approved, which is not a column on event_photos. So the dead path has a working writer and a broken reader, and nothing calls either. WHY THIS IS A DECISION AND NOT A CLEANUP: event_photos is arguably the BETTER schema. It is purpose-built (caption separate from message, is_featured, likes_count) while Option A overloads a general discussions table with a media_url and a type discriminator. The pending migration is not wrong, but it is a commitment, and it is easier to make that call now than after photos start accumulating in event_discussions. LATENT TRAP: src/lib/security/ownership.ts:349 maps photo -> event_photos. No caller currently passes photo as an ownership resourceType, so this is inert today (severity LOW, not a live hole). But the moment anyone wires up delete-my-photo under Option A, the ownership check will look in a table that holds no photos and fail closed — users unable to manage their own content, with nothing obviously wrong in the code. NOTHING WAS DELETED. Removing an entire feature path is a product call, and the dormant path is plausibly the one worth keeping.

userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps). Measured from a real production build: summed the gzipped size of every JS chunk referenced by dist/index.html. Total JS across all 119 chunks is 1,996KB gzipped; the FIRST-PAINT subset was 1,043KB across 30 chunks. PARTIALLY FIXED in commit c29ec4f6: 1043KB -> 610KB (-433KB, -41%) by stopping the prerender step from baking runtime-injected modulepreload links into the shipped HTML. Full root cause in that commit message — briefly, a removeLazyPreloads() plugin existed and looked correct, but (a) it hooked transformIndexHtml, which ALWAYS runs before Vite injects preloads in generateBundle, so it could never have matched, and (b) even once fixed, the prerenderer re-added them by serializing a live DOM in which Vite’s runtime __vitePreload helper had injected them. Both stages now strip, sharing one pattern list, and the build reports the count so a silent regression is visible. REMAINING 610KB, roughly: index entry 160KB, vendor-icons 131KB, vendor-react 88KB, vendor-ui 45KB, vendor-supabase 44KB, plus small route chunks. vendor-icons at 131KB gzipped for an icon library is the most suspicious single line item. NOT ATTEMPTED: chasing the entry chunk or icon tree-shaking, because both change what is statically reachable and need a real LCP measurement to confirm they help rather than just move weight around. Verified no functional regression: smoke suite 7 passed; the 1 failure is the pre-existing get_active_ads PGRST203 (WEB-QA-020), not this change. | CORE WEB VITALS MEASURED 2026-07-18 against a PRODUCTION build (vite preview), each page in a FRESH browser context so every number is a genuine cold load rather than a warm in-app SPA navigation — an earlier pass measured warm navigations and made /events look 5x faster than it is, so the distinction matters. RESULTS: / LCP=2192ms FCP=1648ms CLS=0 transfer=1229KB | /events LCP=348ms FCP=348ms CLS=0.004 transfer=1262KB | /restaurants LCP=460ms FCP=428ms CLS=0 transfer=1462KB. THE HOMEPAGE IS THE OUTLIER — 5x the LCP of other pages at comparable transfer size, so this is not a bytes problem, it is a homepage-specific render problem. CRITICAL CAVEAT ON THE 2192ms: TTFB was 10ms because this is localhost. Effectively all of that 2.2s is client-side work. Real users add TTFB, slower bandwidth and slower CPUs on top, so the <2.5s LCP target in CLAUDE.md is almost certainly ALREADY MISSED in production even though the local number squeaks under it. Do not read this as passing. LCP ELEMENT IDENTIFIED: the hero H1 ("Good Afternoon! Find things to do in Des Moines, right now") paints at 2328ms. It is TEXT, not an image, so LCP is gated on JS execution and hydration, not on downloading a hero asset — which is why the 433KB preload reduction did not move it much. Note the page IS prerendered, yet the largest paint still lands after hydration; worth understanding why the prerendered hero does not count. Secondary candidate at 1652ms is the COOKIE CONSENT BANNER paragraph, which is briefly the largest element on screen. SLOWEST RESOURCES ARE ALL DATA, NOT ASSETS: the six slowest requests are Supabase REST queries (848, 785, 782, 727, 720, 692ms). See WEB-PERF-022 for the duplicate/unbounded events query among them. CHECKED AND RULED OUT: usePlaygrounds uses select("*"), which looked like a WEB-PERF-001 miss, but playgrounds has only 20 columns and NO seo_/geo_/search_vector/geom fields, so there is nothing heavy to project away. Changing it would have been a cosmetic no-op. | ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED 2026-07-18 (commit 94dd972b). The homepage LCP was NOT a bundle-size problem, which is why the earlier 433KB preload reduction barely moved it. First paint on every route was render-blocked on fonts.googleapis.com. index.html ships the correct async pattern (rel=preload + onload flip + noscript fallback), but the prerenderer executes the page in Chromium, the onload handler fires and rewrites rel to "stylesheet" in the live DOM, and page.content() serializes that mutation as the shipped HTML. Measured before: local CSS 10-17ms, font CSS 3035ms, FCP 3204ms — FCP tracked the font request exactly. After: FCP 152ms while the font CSS was still in flight at 227ms, i.e. structurally decoupled. Three post-fix cold runs: FCP 1664/152/212ms, LCP 2208/860/1036ms (run 1 = cold browser, no warm DNS). SAME ROOT CAUSE as the modulepreload bug in c29ec4f6 — prerendering bakes runtime DOM mutations into initial HTML. REMAINING WORK ON THIS STORY IS UNCHANGED: critical-path JS is still 610KB gzipped against a 200KB budget (vendor-icons 131KB, entry chunk 160KB), and that still wants a CI budget check. But the LCP emergency is resolved, so re-prioritise accordingly. ALSO WORTH A THIRD LOOK: the prerenderer has now produced two separate production performance regressions by serializing post-JS DOM state. Consider auditing what ELSE it mutates rather than waiting for the next one to be found by measurement.

userStories.title: The blocking unit-test lane is red on main and has been since the tests were added
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need the vitest lane green, because pr-checks.yml runs it as a blocking step and 5 tests fail, so either PRs are merging over a red required check or the check is not actually enforced.
acceptanceCriteria: npm run test:unit passes
Determine why a blocking check has been failing without anyone acting on it — if the workflow is not actually required on the branch ruleset, make it required

src/contexts/__tests__/AuthContext.test.tsx imports useAuthStatus, which AuthContext does not export. The context exports useAuthState / useAuthFlags / useAuthActions / useAuth — point the test at whichever is the real successor rather than deleting the test

src/components/__tests__/OptimizedImage.test.ts imports canTransform and getTransformedUrl. getTransformedUrl exists but is not exported; canTransform no longer exists at all. See WEB-PERF-021 before making these pass — the assertions encode behaviour the implementation no longer has, so exporting to go green would cement a regression
Extend scripts/check-import-exports.mjs to cover __tests__ directories, which it currently skips — that skip is why this class of breakage is invisible to npm run validate
userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps) while verifying an unrelated dependency bump. 5 failures, all TypeError "X is not a function" — the WEB-QA-001 named-import-with-no-matching-export class, in test files. HISTORY CHECKED: at commit 7e117d85, which introduced OptimizedImage.test.ts, canTransform was already declared as a bare `function canTransform` with no export keyword. So these tests have NEVER passed — they were not broken later, they were merged red. Same shape for AuthContext.test.tsx from 69079b80. WHY IT STAYED INVISIBLE: pr-checks.yml:77 runs `npm run test:unit -- --coverage` and the parity audit recorded that lane as blocking, so a required check has been failing for the life of these files. Worth confirming whether the workflow is actually required in the branch ruleset, because the evidence suggests it is not being enforced. ALSO: scripts/check-import-exports.mjs — the guard written for exactly this bug class — explicitly skips __tests__ directories, so `npm run validate` cannot catch it. That skip was reasonable when written; it is now the blind spot.

userStories.title: External images are proxied through image-transform, which does not resize them
userStories.description: As a visitor, I need external images to load directly, because they are currently routed through an edge function that adds a network hop without reducing bytes.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide the intended behaviour. The WEB-PERF-004 test asserts external URLs serve unchanged, with the stated reason that image-transform does not resize, so proxying adds a hop for zero byte savings
If that reasoning still holds, make getTransformedUrl return external URLs untouched and restore the guard the test was written to provide
If image-transform HAS gained resizing since, update the test and its comment instead, and say so explicitly
Note the load implication: image-transform is one of the public verify_jwt=false endpoints (rate-limited). Routing every external image through it puts real traffic on a public function
Whichever way it goes, the assertions must actually run — see WEB-CI-020
userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-18. src/components/OptimizedImage.tsx getTransformedUrl sends any non-Supabase-Storage URL to /functions/v1/image-transform with width/format/quality params. The test at src/components/__tests__/OptimizedImage.test.ts asserts the opposite ("returns external URLs unchanged (no transform applied)") and documents the reason inline as WEB-PERF-004. This is NOT simply a stale test. The test encodes a deliberate performance decision; the implementation does the thing that decision rejected. Because the test never ran green (see WEB-CI-020), nothing ever flagged the divergence. SEVERITY kept at 3 deliberately: I did not measure how many external images a real page actually loads, so the impact is unquantified. Measure before prioritising — if most images are Supabase Storage URLs, the proxy path is rarely taken and this is minor. NOT FIXED HERE: changing image routing alters what every page requests, and the right answer depends on whether image-transform has gained resizing since WEB-PERF-004. That is a product/infra fact I could not establish from the code alone.

userStories.title: Color contrast fails WCAG AA across the site (71 nodes on /events alone)
userStories.description: As a low-vision visitor, I need text to meet the 4.5:1 contrast ratio CLAUDE.md commits to, because axe reports serious color-contrast violations on every measured public page except /auth.
acceptanceCriteria: Identify the offending token(s) in the Tailwind theme — the volume (71 nodes on one page) points at a small number of shared colours, most likely muted-foreground on a light surface, not 71 separate mistakes
Raise the failing token(s) to 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for large text, and re-run the axe probe on / /events /restaurants /pricing
Fix at the token level, not per-component — a per-instance fix will drift straight back
Verify in dark mode as well; the probe only covered the default theme
Once clean, remove continue-on-error from the accessibility job in e2e.yml so this cannot regress silently (see WEB-CI-021)
userStories.notes: MEASURED 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps) with @axe-core/playwright against a running app, tags wcag2a+wcag2aa+wcag21a+wcag21aa. Per-page violation counts: / = critical/button-name(1) + serious/color-contrast(10); /events = serious/color-contrast(71); /restaurants = critical/button-name(1) + serious/color-contrast(30); /pricing = serious/color-contrast(6); /auth = CLEAN (0). The button-name half is FIXED in commit 6ad76efd (NLPSearchBar icon buttons). Everything remaining is colour contrast. NOT ATTEMPTED, deliberately: contrast is fixed by changing theme tokens, which is a brand/design decision with site-wide visual consequences. Guessing at replacement colours would be worse than reporting the measurement. The concentration (71 nodes on one page) strongly suggests one or two shared tokens rather than scattered one-offs, so the real fix is probably small once someone picks the values. CONTEXT: CLAUDE.md Quality Standards claims "A11y: WCAG 2.1 AA, keyboard nav, ARIA labels, 4.5:1 contrast". The full suite result was 66 passed / 24 failed, so that claim is currently aspirational rather than met.

userStories.title: The accessibility suite runs in CI but cannot fail the build
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need a11y regressions to block, because e2e.yml runs the accessibility suite with continue-on-error: true, so 24 failing tests have never surfaced as a red build.
acceptanceCriteria: Once WEB-UX-030 is fixed, remove continue-on-error from the "Run critical E2E suites" step in .github/workflows/e2e.yml, or split accessibility into its own blocking job
If the suite is too flaky to block on wholesale, gate on the axe checks only (they are deterministic) and leave the keyboard/focus tests advisory — partial enforcement beats none
Record the current failure list as a baseline if a ratchet is preferred, matching the strict-baseline and schema-baseline convention already used here
userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-18. .github/workflows/e2e.yml runs tests/accessibility.spec.ts (plus links-and-buttons, forms, mobile-responsive) under `continue-on-error: true`. The suite is genuinely strict — it asserts zero axe violations against wcag2a/2aa/21a/21aa — but nothing acts on the result. Ran it locally: 66 passed, 24 failed, 11.5 minutes. Failures span axe violations, keyboard navigation, focus visibility, skip links, heading hierarchy (h1 count and level skips), icon-button labels, touch targets, and document titles. This is the same shape as WEB-CI-020 (the unit lane failing under a supposedly blocking check): a quality gate that exists, runs, and cannot fail. Worth treating the two together — the pattern is guards that are present but inert.

userStories.title: Homepage fires two overlapping events queries, one of them unbounded
userStories.description: As a visitor, I need the homepage to fetch events once and with a bound, because it currently issues two near-identical queries and one has no limit, making it the slowest request on the page.
acceptanceCriteria: SmartEventNavigation calls useEvents() with no arguments, so no limit is applied and the query returns every future event (260 today) with the full 24-column projection. Give it the limit it actually renders

Reconcile with AllInclusiveDashboard, which issues its own useEvents call with different filters — different filters mean different react-query keys, so both fetch independently rather than sharing a cache entry
Confirm whether both components need distinct result sets at all, or whether one query can serve both via a shared key
Re-measure: the unbounded query took 848ms and the limited one 785ms, together the two slowest requests on the homepage
No change to the events response shape that shipped mobile binaries read (CLAUDE.md)
userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-18 while measuring Core Web Vitals on a production build (see WEB-PERF-020). Resource timing on a cold homepage load shows two events requests with the same EVENT_LIST_COLUMNS projection and the same date/is_merged/is_hidden filters, differing only in that one carries limit=100 and the other carries no limit at all. Both AllInclusiveDashboard and SmartEventNavigation are mounted on the homepage and each calls useEvents with different filter objects, which produces different query keys, so react-query cannot dedupe them. SEVERITY 3 deliberately: these are parallel XHRs after first paint, so they do not block LCP directly (LCP is the hero H1 at 2328ms, gated on hydration). The cost is server load, bandwidth, and interaction latency once the lists populate — not the headline metric. NOT FIXED HERE: adding a limit changes what SmartEventNavigation renders, and I could not establish from the code how many events it is meant to show. A wrong limit silently truncates a homepage module, which is worse than a slow query.

userStories.title: 12 prerendered routes render no SEOHead, so they ship with no canonical and the site-wide default description
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need every indexable route to declare its own SEO metadata, because a dozen routes ship with no canonical of their own and all 31 share a single meta description.
acceptanceCriteria: Add SEOHead (with an explicit url prop) to: /advertise, /business, /calendar, /deals, /itineraries, /map, /pricing, and the five /events/<city> pages
/business and /map additionally render no h1 at all — add one

Give the five /events/<city> pages distinct titles. They currently all share the same "Events by Location" title, which reads as duplicate content across Altoona, Ankeny, Clive, Johnston and Urbandale
/calendar duplicates the homepage title verbatim
All 31 routes currently share ONE meta description (the static default in index.html). Give at least the top landing routes their own
Re-run the audit and expect: 31 routes, 0 missing canonical, 0 duplicate title groups, 0 duplicate canonical groups
userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps) by auditing the actual prerendered output rather than the source, across all 31 dist/**/index.html files with HTML comments stripped. EXPOSED BY, NOT CAUSED BY, commit 6d1bf574. These 12 routes never rendered SEOHead; they were silently inheriting the hardcoded homepage canonical from index.html. That inherited tag was actively harmful — it told crawlers each route was a duplicate of the homepage — so removing it is a net improvement, since Google self-canonicalizes to the page URL when no tag is present. The underlying gap is that these pages have no SEO identity of their own. STATE AFTER THE FIX: 31 routes, 0 missing title, 0 missing description, 12 missing canonical, 5 missing h1, 0 duplicate canonical groups, 2 duplicate title groups, and all 31 sharing one description. CONTEXT WORTH KEEPING: the prerender step exists specifically to fix soft-404 and "discovered, not indexed" (PROD-SEO-001). Before this fix it emitted 31 pages that each declared the homepage as their canonical — it was actively instructing Google not to index the very routes it was built to get indexed. That is a plausible cause of the original symptom, so re-check Search Console once this deploys.

userStories.title: sitemap-guides.xml is a stale committed artifact; its generator queries a table that does not exist
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need the guides sitemap to reflect reality, because the generator fails on every run and the committed file has not been regenerated since it was first added.
acceptanceCriteria: generateGuidesSitemap queries public.guides, which does not exist (42P01). Decide whether guides live in seasonal_guides (which DOES exist) or are static routes, and point the generator at the real source

On failure the function returns null WITHOUT writing the file, so the stale public/sitemap-guides.xml silently survives. Make a generator failure either fail the build or write an empty-but-valid sitemap — silently shipping stale data is the worst of the three options
Verify the 11 URLs currently in the file still resolve. /guides and /guides/:slug are real routes (App.tsx:431, 471), so they are probably valid, but nothing has checked since the file was committed
Extend scripts/check-schema-usage.mjs to cover scripts/ as well as src/ — this exact bug class is what that guard exists to catch, and it is currently blind to build scripts
userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-07-18 (claude/prd-loop-schema-gaps) while auditing sitemap contents. Every `npm run generate-sitemaps` run prints "Error fetching guides: relation public.guides does not exist" (42P01) and continues. Because the generator returns null before writing, public/sitemap-guides.xml is whatever was committed in 851158c4 and has never been regenerated. It is referenced from sitemap-index.xml, so Google is being handed a hand-frozen file. SEVERITY 3: the 11 URLs are plausibly still valid (both /guides and /guides/:slug are live routes), so this is probably stale-but-harmless today rather than broken. The real risk is the silent-failure pattern — a generator that errors, keeps going, and ships last-known-good data looks identical to one that works. RELATED: this is the same missing-table class as WEB-QA-018, and it is invisible to scripts/check-schema-usage.mjs because that guard only scans src/. The sitemap generator is exactly the kind of build-time code where a silent schema mismatch does damage without anyone seeing a stack trace. Note there IS a seasonal_guides table in the schema, and the route component is SeasonalGuide, so the intended source may simply be a rename that the script never followed.
